A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MR-LFADS study. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-F are readable and matchable despite pagination and display changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-fitting results on 37 synthetic datasets and original analyses and perturbation predictions using mouse electrophysiology data (Sections 4-5).

after.justification: v2 retains these original synthetic-data and electrophysiology results, with additional input-norm reporting in the appendix.

M1.justification: The MR-LFADS architecture, causal inference procedure, communication variants, output distributions, and structured KL objective remain unchanged. Figure 1 labeling corrections do not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the memory network, pass-decision network, 35 random task-trained networks, and the same mouse recording sessions and perturbation scenarios. Appendix D clarifies stimulus channels without adding tasks.

E2.justification: RRR, MR-SDS, mp-srSLDS, and the experiment-specific MR-LFADS variants retain their membership in corresponding comparisons. The new input-norm displays use existing comparators.

E3.justification: The stated data splits, neuron holdout, model configurations, training budgets, and perturbation procedures are retained. Added descriptions of cross-validation, decoder training trials, and timing sampling document existing experiments without establishing a protocol revision.

E4.justification: Figures S1b and S2b extend the diagnostic evidence with region-wise input-norm heatmaps across models, supplementing the communication-norm comparisons. The existing input-specification ablation, communication-source comparisons, KL-channel analysis, and SVD analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 2 now defines the IQR boxes and 1.5-IQR whiskers, and Figure S5 identifies its shading as standard deviation across seeds. The relevant repeated-run counts were already reported; these clarifications do not establish additional runs.

E6.justification: Figure S1 adds maximum input norms of 76, 175, 60, 188, and 0 for MR-LFADS(R), MR-LFADS(S), MR-SDS, mp-srSLDS, and RRR, respectively. Figure S2 removes its listed maximum message norms. Existing communication heatmaps, headline findings, and Figure 4 p-values are retained.

T1.justification: Equations 1-20 and the mathematical reasoning are retained. Appendix E.2 clarifies the analyzed region and renames the message projection W_m to W_mu_m, without changing the SVD argument or introducing a proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and central empirical claims remain unchanged. Section 6 adds the broader contribution-level proposition that the three design principles may also support alternative local-dynamics architectures.

C2.justification: Section 6 strengthens the shared-unobserved-input limitation from a confound that likely cannot be resolved to one that cannot be resolved from passive neural activity alone. It also adds discussion of applicability to alternative architectures.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 specifies that the post hoc decoder is fitted on training trials and evaluated on validation trials. Appendix D newly specifies independent uniform timing draws, while Appendix B.1 documents the revised display normalization and sigmoid scaling.

R1.justification: Section 2 drops Steinmetz et al. (2019) from the RRR citation cluster while retaining that work elsewhere and in the bibliography. The cited-work inventory and broader static-versus-dynamic research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose revisions, adds explanatory sentences, and gives Experiments 1 and 3 more descriptive headings. The main section sequence and appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Effectome drawings replace thresholded, clipped arrow widths with normalized color intensity. Figures S1-S2 gain input-norm rows; S4 sorts channels by magnitude; several figures receive larger labels, clarified captions, and layout adjustments. The existing figure and table set is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility through clearer training-versus-validation documentation and makes statistical displays and effectome normalization easier to interpret. Added input-norm reporting provides useful diagnostic detail. Although Figure S2 loses its absolute normalization values, the documentation and presentation gains support a limited net improvement while the central scientific evidence remains stable.
